newsitem.title: USA: BG&E, PEPCO fault merger analysis.
newsitem.headline: BG&E, PEPCO fault merger analysis.

text.p: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission made mistakes in its analysis of competition in the energy market that would be served by a merger of Baltimore Gas and Electric Co and Potomac Electric Power Co, according to economist Joe Pace.
The commission raised concerns last month that the merged company, Constellation Energy, would be able to dominate its market, partly because of area transmission constraints.
The FERC also questioned whether it was fair to include the whole Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) power pool, which includes 10 utilities, in the market evaluation.
The companies defended their merger plan in a filing this week responding to the commission's questions.

"When the (FERC's) errors are corrected, in all cases, the (indexes) pass the market concentration screens" set by the Justice Department and Federal Trade Commission merger guidelines, Pace, a managing director at Law & Economics Consulting Group, Inc, said in the filing.

He said the commission had incorrectly included certain utilities in its analysis of the market concentration in the existing markets in three areas, leading to wrong conclusions that the market concentration would increase after the merger.
"Second, the narrowest plausible relevant market for nonfirm energy includes all PJM members plus the Allegheny Power System and the Consolidated Edison Co," Pace said.

He said proposals by the PJM power pool to set a single transmission charge for the whole network would effectively expand the market in which Constellation Energy would compete, drawing in five more utilities in New York, Virginia and Ohio.
Pace said that in a few hours of the year, high demand limited PJM members' ability to transfer power in the pool but Constellation could not take advantage of those constraints.
"In these circumstances, BGE and PEPCO are among the suppliers potentially blocked from making additional energy sales ... and their competitive significance therefore is diminished," he said.

The FERC last month called for a hearing record on the proposed merger to be completed by November 1, aiming to issue a final decision on the plan early next year. The companies said that they did not expect the delay to thwart their plans to merge next spring.
